name: Fenugreek
short: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort is commonest; allergy and hypoglycaemia are reported. A review advises against use in pregnancy (animal studies) and says teratogenic effects were reported in humans.
text: A scoping review of 60 articles found that the most common adverse effect of fenugreek taken by mouth was mild gastrointestinal discomfort; of the clinical trials it covered, 14 reported adverse effects, 23 reported none and 13 gave no information on adverse effects, and the authors judged most effects mild and self-limiting. Other effects reported in that review were hypoglycaemia, possible low potassium, allergic reactions (10 case reports or case series described allergy or hypersensitivity), a maple syrup odour in the urine, sweat or skin of infants and mothers, and interactions with certain medications, which the abstract does not name. A toxicology review advises that people with peanut or chickpea allergy, or chronic asthma, avoid fenugreek because of possible cross-reactivity, and says it is not recommended during pregnancy, a caution it bases on animal studies in rats, mice and rabbits showing testicular toxicity and anti-fertility effects in males and anti-fertility, anti-implantation and abortifacient activity in females. The review also says that teratogenic effects, from congenital malformations to death, were reported in humans, rodents, rabbits and chicks; the abstract does not say what kind of human reports these were. The review adds that accumulating evidence suggests fenugreek may have neurodevelopmental, neurobehavioural and neuropathological side effects; the abstract does not say whether that evidence comes from animal studies or from people. A single case report describes a raised INR in a patient on warfarin who said she was taking a variety of natural products, including boldo and fenugreek; the INR returned to normal after she stopped the suspected products and the interaction was seen a second time when both products were reintroduced, so the effect cannot be attributed to fenugreek alone.
